title: Vector peakon equations and isospectral flows in Clifford algebras
authors: Andrew N. W. Hone, Vladimir S. Novikov, Jacek Szmigielski
abstract: Starting from a spectral problem posed in a Clifford algebra with $d$ generators and Euclidean signature, we study an integrable, coupled system of PDEs that can be viewed as a vector perturbation of the Camassa--Holm equation with residual orthogonal symmetry. In the two-component case $d=2$, we show that the travelling wave solutions correspond to a Liouville integrable Hamiltonian system with two degrees of freedom, making use of a reciprocal transformation linking the coupled PDEs to a symmetry of the Hirota--Satsuma system. We also present a symmetry classification of all integrable two-component perturbations of Camassa--Holm, and find that besides the $d=2$ system analyzed here, the coupled 2CH system studied by Olver and Rosenau (as well as by Chen, Liu and Zhang, and Falqui), and equations related to either of those systems by Miura transformations, we also obtain a new system that (to the best of our knowledge) has not been reported previously. For the case of an arbitrary number of components $d$, we additionally investigate the short-pulse (high-frequency) regime, in which the limiting dynamics are governed by a vector-valued Hunter-Saxton type system. Furthermore, we provide a detailed analysis of the corresponding measure-valued (weak) solutions associated with this system.
summary: This work analyzes complex, multi-component generalizations of the Camassa–Holm equation using Clifford algebras. It establishes deep connections between these PDEs and integrable Hamiltonian systems by employing advanced mathematical tools like spectral theory and reciprocal transformations. The research yields explicit solutions for peakon dynamics in the high-frequency limit, providing a comprehensive classification of related integrable models.
main_problem: The study investigates integrable, coupled systems of partial differential equations (PDEs) that represent vector perturbations of the Camassa–Holm equation within the mathematical framework of Clifford algebras.
main_result: The authors provide a complete classification of integrable two-component CH perturbations and derive explicit solutions for multi-peakon dynamics in the high-frequency limit, showing connections to Liouville integrable Hamiltonian systems.
method: The analysis employs advanced techniques including spectral theory on Clifford algebras, reciprocal transformations, Lax pair formulations, and reduction to finite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems via travelling wave assumptions.
model_or_system: The core model is a $d$-component vector PDE system derived from an isospectral deformation problem in $	ext{C}\ell(W)$, generalizing the scalar Camassa–Holm equation. Specific focus is placed on the two-component case ($d=2$) and its high-frequency (Hunter-Saxton) limit.
key_observables: Conserved functionals/densities, peakon positions ($x_N$), amplitudes ($m_{ij}$), and the Weyl function $W(\lambda, t)$.
important_parameters: The number of components ($d$), the arbitrary constant $\alpha$, and the specific parameters defining the initial conditions for multi-peakons.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes zero background solutions when studying travelling waves, and integrability is defined by the existence of an infinite hierarchy of local higher symmetries.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of two-component peakon positions and amplitudes for the HS2 system, showing asymptotic periodicity or divergence. Other figures show Liouville tori projections related to the Hamiltonian reduction.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general integrable structure via Clifford algebras and symmetries (symmetries classification) to analyzing specific reductions like the $d=2$ case using reciprocal transformations, culminating in explicit solutions for multi-peakon dynamics in the high-frequency limit.
why_interesting: While focused on classical PDEs, the rigorous mathematical machinery—integrability theory, spectral methods, and Hamiltonian reduction—is highly relevant to understanding non-linear wave phenomena in quantum field theories or effective descriptions of many-body systems where continuum limits are taken.
